title: Graphics card, power supply, cooling and case

videos.script: The first lesson was the three parts that do the work. This one is the three that let them. {{four}} A graphics card draws what you see. A power supply feeds everything. Cooling carries away the heat that feeding everything produces. And the case holds the four of them in a shape that lets air through. {{parts}} None of those is glamorous and every one of them is where a machine actually fails. A processor almost never dies. A power supply does, and when it does it can take other things with it. Cooling does not fail so much as quietly stop being enough, and the symptom is a machine that is fast for ten minutes and slow afterwards. {{fail}} So the through-line here is different from the last lesson. That one was about where work waits. This one is about where a computer's limits are physical — watts, degrees and airflow — and about the two numbers that people get wrong in opposite directions: buying far more power supply than they need, and far less cooling. {{limits}} We finish on the one question worth asking before any of it: do you need a graphics card at all.
